samples.summary: `structuralEditable` was not updated for the `role: 'container'` widening, so the outline still predicts the OLD resolveNode answer and no metadata field expresses container-editability at all
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/src/server/extract.mjs:552-556 computes `structuralEditable = scope==='static' && tag!=='#returns' && owner===node && !returnedJsx.includes(node)` — i.e. exactly the `role: 'target'` guard set. It is documented as "MIRRORS resolveNode(…, {requireStatic: true}), GUARD FOR GUARD" (extract.mjs:537) and as "a prediction of what resolveNode(…, {requireStatic: true}) will answer" (docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:907-925). After this diff, `resolveNode(sf, a, {requireStatic:true, role:'container'})` returns `located: true` for the two shapes the flag reports as `false` — a returned root element and a `{cond && <div/>}` element — which are precisely the nodes `applyLayoutInsert` (inject.mjs:602) now accepts as parents. `SceneNodeMeta` (packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:116) has only the one boolean, so a client has no field from which to enable "insert child into this node" or to re-offer the undo of a remove inside a component root — the exact data-loss case the diff's own doc (engine.md:801-806) says the widening exists to fix. The drift-guard test only exercises the default role (packages/design-editor/test/server/extract.test.mjs:353-357), so the half of the contract that changed is unasserted and will drift silently.

samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:910 exports `nodeAt(_sf, root, path)` and its test asserts "walkJsx feeds the client outline; nodeAt is how a write finds its target" (packages/design-editor/test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:564). The writer that landed does not call it: inject.mjs:753-762 defines its own `nodeAtPath`, so `nodeAt` now has no production consumer and the walk exists twice. extract.mjs:506-509 states the identity of the numbering across modules is "the contract; two implementations of it would let an edit land on the wrong node with nothing to catch it". Either extend `nodeAt` to return the scope and call it, or drop `nodeAt`.

verdict.reason: The absence claim has a direct counterexample. Container-editability IS expressible from published SceneNodeMeta fields: after the widening, `role: 'container'` refuses only (a) the synthetic returns root (jsx-nodes.mjs:838, tag `#returns`) and (b) non-static scope (jsx-nodes.mjs:844-853). Both discriminators are emitted per node — `tag` at extract.mjs:528 and `scope` at extract.mjs:536 — and `scope` is declared on the public interface at types.ts:114 with its op semantics documented at types.ts:110-113 ("static — all ops allowed; iteration/callback — layout-props only"). So `scope === 'static' && tag !== '#returns'` is a guard-for-guard container prediction available to any client. Additionally, `structuralEditable` has not drifted from the contract it documents: extract.mjs:537 and engine.md:907-925 name `resolveNode(…, {requireStatic: true})`, which is the default `'target'` role (jsx-nodes.mjs:792, :859), and the target-role guards at jsx-nodes.mjs:864 and :887 are unchanged (`!asContainer && …`), so the flag and the drift-guard test at extract.test.mjs:353-357 still agree with the resolver call they cite. Finally there is no caller to break: `structuralEditable`, `SceneNodeMeta` and `analyzeNodes` have no references outside packages/design-editor's own src/tests/docs, so no site bypasses or misreads the changed contract. The residue is at most a missing convenience flag or doc nuance, not a blocking blast-radius defect.
